inputs.original_text: South Portland’s schools are facing another major budget shortfall, with more than 70 positions set to be cut. Families and taxpayers deserve more than apologies: they deserve to know how the district got here and why classroom needs weren’t protected. Schools should put students, parents, and basic education first—not let administrative priorities crowd out the people doing the work. It’s time for honest accounting, disciplined spending, and real accountability.
inputs.modified_text: South Portland’s schools are facing a major shortfall, and more than 70 positions are set to be cut. That means real consequences for students and the people who teach and support them—not just a line in a budget. The district owes families a clear account of how it reached this point, but “discipline” can’t mean balancing the books by putting the burden on classroom workers and children. We need transparent decisions, protection for basic education, and accountability for the priorities that left these jobs vulnerable.
